close_reason: Applied the reviewer's stable workaround: collapsed the three duplicate 'if O::TYPE_NAME == CalendarEvent' sites in create/update/destroy into one Inner::maintain_indexes_after_set helper. The principled fix (foundation JmapObject trait revision) is filed separately at JMAP-934u — it requires a workspace-foundation change with propagation through every extension server, which is out of scope for a single calendars-server review bead.
description:
memory.rs uses string equality on O::TYPE_NAME inside generic methods to specialise behaviour:

  - memory.rs:282-284 (seed_object — recompute when type is CalendarEvent)
  - memory.rs:536-546 (query_objects — extract inCalendar filter only for CalendarEvent)
  - memory.rs:700-702 (create_object — recompute when type is CalendarEvent)
  - memory.rs:758-760 (update_object — same)
  - memory.rs:788-790 (destroy_object — same)

Each branch reads:
  if O::TYPE_NAME == "CalendarEvent" {
      inner.recompute_calendars_with_events(account_id.as_ref());
  }

The point of a generic 'fn create_object<O: SetObject + Send + Sync>' is to be polymorphic over the type. Branching on the type-name string at runtime defeats that — the compiler cannot prove the branch is reachable from every O, and the runtime check fires on every call. This is the same kind of dynamic-type smell that match-on-Any has in code that should be using generics.

Canonical jmap-mail-server has the identical pattern (memory.rs:690, :741, :763, :780 — 'if O::TYPE_NAME == "Mailbox"', 'if O::TYPE_NAME == "Email"', 'if O::TYPE_NAME == "EmailSubmission"'), so this is a workspace-wide pattern, not a calendars-only divergence. Per workspace AGENTS.md canonical-template rule, the fix is to change the canonical first.

Two idiomatic alternatives:
(a) Add a type-introspection method to JmapObject (the foundation trait): 'fn after_set_hook(backend: &mut MemoryInner, account_id: &str)'. CalendarEvent and Email override it; other types get a no-op default. Dispatch is via the trait, not a string compare.
(b) Move the per-type post-write index maintenance out of the generic create/update/destroy and into per-type wrappers (already partially present as create_calendar_event/update_calendar_event for scheduling). The generic /set never recomputes; only the per-type wrapper does.

Workaround that's stable: add the string-equality check to a single private helper 'fn after_write<O: JmapObject>(inner: &mut Inner, account_id: &str)' that does the dispatch once instead of inlining the check at every call site. That at least colocates the type-specific logic.

Option (a) is the principled fix and would belong in jmap-server (the foundation crate). Option (b) is the lower-effort workaround.
title: MemoryBackend dispatches on O::TYPE_NAME string equality across generic methods
